messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache eviction rate spiking + continuous-batching amplification detected in us-west-2. Paging eng-oncall @alex_white @maria_g. Incident ID: INC-20260312-87

alex_white: I'm on it. Pulling up metrics now. Any customer impact seen yet?

maria_g: 5xxs on /generate up ~3% overall but concentrated on two tenants — acme-inc and looplabs. Latency tail increasing.

sanjay: Heatmap and top-ten tenants attached. Looks like runaway prefix cache growth started ~03:50 after the continuous batch flag change rolled yesterday.

jin: Logs show the flag `continuous_batch_v2` set `adaptive: true, base_window_ms: 60`. That adaptive behavior might be over-shrinking windows under high prefix churn.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline: continuous_batch_v2 rollout -> stable completed @ 2026-03-12T04:15Z (pipeline-id: dp-3345).

alex_white: Mitigation plan — quick: 1) soften global batch aggressiveness 2) per-tenant overrides for affected customers 3) canary rollback path if needed. Who can flip flags?

maria_g: I can. Proposing immediate global soft-rollback: set `base_window_ms=100` and `adaptive=false` to stop amplification while we assess.

sanjay: Agreed. Also set per-tenant caps for acme-inc and looplabs to avoid cache blowup. Commands below.

sanjay: ```
# global soft rollback
redwoodctl featureflag update continuous_batch_v2 --set base_window_ms=100 --set adaptive=false --env production
# per-customer tighter window + max batch
redwoodctl featureflag update continuous_batch_v2 --customer acme-inc --set base_window_ms=200 --set max_batch=8
redwoodctl featureflag update continuous_batch_v2 --customer looplabs --set base_window_ms=200 --set max_batch=8
```

maria_g: Running the global command now. Rolling a 30s canary to 10% of hosts, then widen if metrics improve.

ops-bot: Flag change accepted. Rollout ID: fl-98765. Canary targets: hostpool-prod-a -> starting.

alex_white: I'll watch `kv.evictions_per_min`, `serving.latency.p95`, and `kv.kv_memory_bytes` per-tenant. Also tracking token-efficiency metrics.

jin: Can we set a hard per-tenant KV cap for acme-inc while the flag change lands? Quick command: 
```
redwoodctl kv policy set --tenant acme-inc --max_kv_mb 512
```

maria_g: Set caps for acme-inc and looplabs. Confirmed.

sanjay: Canary metrics: evictions down ~70% on canary hosts after ~60s. Latency p95 for canary hosts down from 820ms -> 230ms.

alex_white: :thumbsup: Good signal. If stable for 5m we go global. Any downstream side effects expected?

maria_g: Minor throughput dip for tiny tenants (~5%), but no error spike. Plan: staged global at 5m.

ops-bot: Rollout progressed: 10% -> 50% -> 100% within 2m.

maria_g: Global change finished. Aggregate evictions down ~60%, us-west-2 region recovered. acme-inc still shows a small tail on very large requests; keeping per-tenant cap.

jin: Post-incident recommendations: add a load test scenario with high prefix churn and variable batching; add alert for eviction_rate > 3x baseline; and enforce safe lower-bound for base_window_ms (no less than 50ms).

alex_white: Agree. Ops/infra follow-ups: update runbook, add canary guardrails for featureflag changes that affect batching, and add per-tenant observability for KV size.

maria_g: I'll draft an incident summary for SRE + CS with timeline, affected tenants (acme-inc, looplabs), commands executed, mitigations, and next steps.

kevin: Taking over watch for next 2h @kevin. Will monitor dashboards and coordinate with CS if they see tickets.

alex_white: Leaving runbook notes: 
```
Runbook entry: KV-amplification-2026-03-12
Steps:
  - Check kv.evictions_per_min and serving.latency.p95
  - If evictions > 2x baseline: set continuous_batch_v2 base_window_ms=100, adaptive=false
  - For affected tenants: set max_kv_mb cap and per-tenant base_window_ms=200
  - Monitor canary for 5m before global rollout
  - Escalate to infra if evictions do not drop after 10m
```

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-20260312-87 mitigated -> monitoring. Paging closed, oncall handoff to @kevin noted.

maria_g: Filed CS tickets for acme-inc and looplabs, added mitigation details and expected customer impact. Will post the incident summary link here when ready.

kevin: I'll keep an eye and tag in any new alerts. Thanks team.
